extra.message: Flask debug mode enabled on network-exposed interface — If Werkzeug's interactive debugger is reachable, an attacker who triggers an unhandled exception can get a PIN-protected (often brute-forceable) console allowing arbitrary code execution; at minimum it leaks stack traces, source code, and environment details. [verified: app.py:24 binds to 0.0.0.0 with debug=True, enabling the Werkzeug interactive debugger network-wide with no compensating control, allowing RCE via the debugger console on any unhandled exception.]

SQL Injection via username parameter in /sqlivuln — Attacker can inject SQL to bypass authentication, exfiltrate all rows from the USERS table (credentials), or perform blind/error-based SQLi using the reflected exception message. [verified: username is directly f-string interpolated into SQL with no parameterization or sanitization, and exceptions leak to the client, confirming exploitable SQLi with no compensating control.]

Server-Side Template Injection via mathexp parameter — Full remote code execution on the server via Jinja2 SSTI payloads (e.g. accessing __globals__/__builtins__ to spawn a shell). [verified: User-controlled mathexp is directly string-concatenated into a Jinja2 Template and rendered with no sanitization or sandboxing, enabling classic SSTI RCE payloads like {{ self.__init__.__globals__.__builtins__.__import__('os').popen('id').read() }}.]

Local File Inclusion via filename parameter — Arbitrary file read on the server filesystem, disclosure of sensitive files (config, credentials, source code). [verified: User-controlled filename from JSON body flows directly into open() with no sanitization or path restriction, matching the priority CWE-22 vuln class in the threat model.]

Server-Side Request Forgery via imagelink parameter — Attacker can make the server issue arbitrary outbound requests to internal services (cloud metadata endpoints, internal network) and read the response, enabling internal network reconnaissance/exfiltration. [verified: imagelink flows unvalidated from JSON body into requests.get() with no allowlist, SSRF is the intentionally vulnerable RFI endpoint per threat model.]

Host Header Injection reflected into HTML response — Attacker can poison password-reset or generated links via a spoofed Host header, or inject markup/script if reflected in an HTML context (link poisoning / XSS). [verified: Host header is attacker-controlled and reflected verbatim into the msg field with no escaping (hhi.py:12,18); however since this is a JSON API response (not rendered HTML), actual XSS impact depends on a client rendering msg unescaped, so severity is more content-injection than direct XSS.]
